units.title: ADR-050 — A two-line label must straddle a diamond's midline (2026-07-30)
units.content:
# ADR-050 — A two-line label must straddle a diamond's midline (2026-07-30)

Context: On the AI Brain page the only decision diamond that carries a subtitle,
"Did it pass?" / "Teacher grades held-out exams", had its subtitle crossing the
orange outline on both sides. Measured before the fix, at the wide geometry in
Japanese: subtitle 177.88 user units against 158.78 available, so **9.55 units of
overhang per side**. Compact/Japanese overhung by 1.05.

Cause: `FlowBox` placed the subtitle at `mid + gap` for every shape. That is correct
for a rectangle or a cylinder, which are the same width at every height, but a
diamond is only full width at its vertical midline and tapers to a point above and
below. At `dy = 13.5` of a 37-unit half-height the shape has already given up 36% of
its width, so the label was being drawn where the box no longer existed. The title
was fine only because it is short.

Decision: when a decision has a subtitle, straddle the midline — title at
`mid - (gap/2 + 1.5)`, sub at `mid + (gap/2 + 1.5)` — so both lines sit in the widest
band instead of one hanging into the taper. Non-diamond shapes keep the original
slightly-low placement, which reads better inside a constant-width box. The diamond's
own geometry is untouched, deliberately: extending the tips to gentle the taper would
have been the other fix, but the arrow into a diamond already terminates 5 units
inside its top tip (`to: y + rowH - 3` vs a tip at `y + rowH - 8`), so growing the
tips would have widened a pre-existing overlap into a visible one and required
threading the next stage's kind into `FlowArrow`. Not worth it for a text-placement
bug.

**Straddling alone was not enough, and the first verification of it was wrong.** It was
checked by computing the diamond's width at the text's *centre line* and comparing that
to `getComputedTextLength()`, which reported 8.19 units of margin and looked clean in a
3x capture. But a line of text has height, and the binding constraint is its **lower
corners**, which sit ~6.6 units below the centre where the diamond has narrowed
further. Re-tested with `SVGGeometryElement.isPointInFill` against the real path, using
all four corners of `getBBox()`: the bottom two corners were still outside in both
locales (EN sub 159.97 units, JA 177.88, against ~150 usable at that height). A
validation subagent caught this independently.

So the subtitle was **shortened** as well, the remedy ADR-043/044 already used for the
116-unit phone branch box: "Teacher grades held-out exams" → "Graded by the teacher"
(159.97 → 91.07 units) and "教師モデルが持ち出し不可試験を採点" → "教師モデルが採点"
(177.88 → 65.11). "Held-out exams" is not lost; the prose above the chart already says
the exams are commits the cheap model has never seen.

Consequences: All four `getBBox()` corners of both the title and the subtitle now test
inside the diamond path, in EN and JA, at both the wide and compact geometries — the
strict test, not the centre-line one. The other four charts contain no decision with a
subtitle, so nothing else moved. Production build clean.

Lesson: to check text against a non-rectangular shape, test the text's bounding-box
corners with `isPointInFill` against the actual path. Comparing text length to the
shape's width at the text's centre line silently passes labels that visibly cross the
outline, and comparing against the shape's *bounding box* is looser still.

units.title: ADR-051 — GSAP applies vars in reverse, so never mix `inset` with `left`/`top` (2026-07-30)
units.content:
# ADR-051 — GSAP applies vars in reverse, so never mix `inset` with `left`/`top` (2026-07-30)

Context: A validation subagent found that the mobile card-expand opened from the
viewport's top-left corner rather than from the tapped card. Confirmed independently
by sampling the overlay per animation frame and by a MutationObserver on its `style`
attribute. Before the fix the overlay's first painted frame was `[0, 0, 357, 478]`
while the tapped card sat at `[20, 451.23, 350, 404.75]`; `el.style.left` was `auto`
and `left` stayed 0 for all ~80 frames of every open. The error equals the card's
distance from the viewport origin, so it grew with scroll position — up to ~451px.

Cause: the open did

```js
gsap.set(el, { autoAlpha: 1, inset: 'auto', left: origin.left, top: origin.top, ... })
```

GSAP's CSSPlugin builds its PropTween list by **prepending**, so vars are applied in
the reverse of the order written. `inset: 'auto'` therefore landed *after* `left` and
`top` and reset both — `inset` is a shorthand for all four offsets. The subsequent
`.to(el, { left: 0, top: 0, ... })` then read its start values from computed style,
which for `position: fixed` with `inset: auto` resolves to the static position `0,0`,
so left/top tweened 0 → 0 and never moved.

Decision: set `right: 'auto'` and `bottom: 'auto'` explicitly instead of the `inset`
shorthand. Those are distinct properties from `left`/`top`, so no application order can
clobber the origin rect. The reduced-motion branch keeps `inset: 0` — it pairs it with
`width/height: 'auto'` and sets no left/top, so there is nothing to overwrite.

Consequences: The overlay's first style write now reads exactly the card's rect —
`left=20px top=388px width=350px height=426px right=auto bottom=auto` against a
measured origin of `[20, 387.98, 350, 425.81]` — and the open still ends at
`[0, 0, 390, 844]`, the full viewport. Verified on two cards at two scroll positions.

Why four previous ADRs missed it: the close was never affected, because it does not
touch `inset`, and it lands within 0.42px. ADR-046's per-frame sampling compared each
clone child against its original — all *relative* measurements, which stay correct even
when the whole overlay starts in the wrong place. Absolute origin was never asserted.
Any future check of this animation must compare the overlay's own first frame against
the origin card's rect.

shorthand. Those are distinct properties from `left`/`top`, so no application order can
clobber the origin rect. The reduced-motion branch keeps `inset: 0` — it pairs it with
`width/height: 'auto'` and sets no left/top, so there is nothing to overwrite.

touch `inset`, and it lands within 0.42px. ADR-046's per-frame sampling compared each

the origin card's rect.

units.title: ADR-052 — Japanese is a real locale, not a translation layer (2026-07-30)
units.content:
# ADR-052 — Japanese is a real locale, not a translation layer (2026-07-30)

Context: The ADR-049 rewrite fixed two projects' copy but a validation sweep showed the
Japanese side of the site was only partly localized, and that three projects' Japanese
described a different product from their English.

Decision, in the order the problems bite:

1. **`document.documentElement.lang` now follows the locale.** `index.html` ships
   `lang="en"` and nothing ever changed it, so a Japanese visitor got a fully translated
   page still declaring itself English, and screen readers read Japanese with an English
   voice. Set in the same effect that persists the preference.

2. **Badges are localized.** `badge` had no Japanese counterpart, so all six cards *and*
   all six detail heroes showed `live app` / `in progress` / `research project` /
   `long-term project` / `student PWA` / `macOS utility` on an otherwise Japanese page.
   Added `badgeJa` to every project and a `badgeLabel(project, locale)` helper used by
   both render sites, falling back to `badge` if a translation is ever missing.

3. **Strings that were hardcoded English are now keys.** The footer's role and city and
   the contact card's "Email" (which said "Email" while the hero said "メール" for the
   same action, on the same page) became `footerRole`, `footerCity` and the existing
   `t.email`. `building` was "AIツールを開発中" against an English "Building AI agent
   tools" — the Japanese had quietly dropped "agent", which is the whole point of the
   line.

4. **Three projects' locales were reconciled.** WebDrop, Tutor-System and TokaiHub had
   Japanese card copy and taglines that were stale marketing register (feature dumps,
   モダンな, ネイティブアプリのような) against plain English. Worse, **WebDrop's Japanese
   advertised バンプペアリング — bump pairing — a mechanism the English never claims.**
   Both sides now say the same thing.

5. **The remaining AI-tells were removed from the four projects ADR-049 did not touch**,
   plus two residues in the pair it did: ClaudeShot's "keep the utility practical for
   daily use", Tutor's "Fast teaching stays in the foreground.", TokaiHub's "email
   aliases keep login familiar" and its `with…plus` weld of onboarding to theming,
   WebDrop's "when those sensors are not" (an ellipsis that never completes), AI Brain's
   tricolon and four-clause chain, and the Internship Portal's "does two things"
   followed by four. The home intro's opening tricolon went too — it was the first
   sentence a visitor read.

6. **The last two em dashes in user-facing strings** were the card `aria-label`
   ("WebDrop — View details", on all six cards in both locales, so screen-reader-only
   and easy to miss) and the ErrorBoundary copy.

Consequences: Swept 28 route × locale × breakpoint combinations at 390x844 and
1280x900 over CDP: **zero problems** — `lang` correct in all four locale/breakpoint
pairs, all six badges Japanese under `ja`, no em dash in any rendered string, no
horizontal overflow, no clipped titles, no broken images, no `.pd-block` stuck hidden,
flow-chart connectors present on all 24 detail combos, all diamond labels inside their
path, 0 console errors and 0 responses >= 400. The mobile expand still writes the
tapped card's exact rect on open (ADR-051 holds). Production build clean.

units.title: ADR-053 — Copy consistency pass, and the Japanese spacing trap (2026-08-02)
units.content:
# ADR-053 — Copy consistency pass, and the Japanese spacing trap (2026-08-02)

Context: `git pull` brought one automated commit (`c403cf6..3403921`) touching only
`public/assets/contributions.json` — the rolling window slid forward, dropping
2025-08-01/02 and appending 2026-07-31 and 2026-08-01, total 583 → 586. A bug sweep of
the whole site was run on top of it. Most of the sweep's agents died on a session
limit; the copy dimension completed and its nine findings were verified by hand
afterwards, since every automated verifier had also died.

The pulled data itself is correct and needed no change: 364 cells, exactly 52 weeks,
contiguous, no duplicates, first cell 2025-08-03 is a Sunday and last 2026-08-01 a
Saturday, `total` equals the sum of counts. The 12 month labels were re-derived
independently against the component's own bucketing and every one sits over a column
that really contains that month; the trailing single-day Aug 2026 is correctly dropped
by the `span >= 3` filter, so there is no duplicate "Aug".

Decisions — nine copy defects fixed, all confirmed against source before touching:

1. The Internship Portal overview enumerated four tracker states and the feature bullet
   five, two paragraphs apart. The overview no longer enumerates at all; the bullet owns
   the list.
2. AI Brain's flow introduced "the gym", a term used in no other rendered string (the
   overview calls the same thing a loop), and alternated "a teacher model" / "the
   teacher" / "Graded by the teacher". Settled on "the loop" and "the teacher model"
   throughout, diagram included.
3. Tutor-System's Japanese used three words for one concept — バックグラウンドジョブ,
   背景, バックグラウンド処理 — where 背景 is the picture-background sense, not a running
   process. Also 前景チューター, a calque of an English term the English never defines.
   Both sides now say it plainly.
4. Stray ASCII spaces inside 「Markdownの Brain」 and 「Cognitoメール OTP」, inconsistent
   with the same words written unspaced on those very pages.
5. WebDrop's decision diamond was the only one of four not phrased as a question in
   Japanese (「近接を確認」, which also duplicated the system-map label directly above the
   chart). Now 「十分に近いか」.
6. English copy carried two tokens an English-only reader cannot read (履歴書, 職務経歴書)
   with no gloss; it now names the formats in English while the Japanese keeps the real
   names. "centre" was the single en-GB spelling among catalog / signaling / enrollment /
   localize.
7. `t.tech` served both an inline card label (where the trailing colon is right) and an
   `<h2>` section heading (where it is not). Split into `tech` and `techHeading`.
8. The footer read "1,338visitors" in the text stream. Added the space to the English
   unit only — Japanese takes none.
9. Three English grammar slips: two compound subjects with singular verbs, one missing
   article with a comparative that had no comparand.

Then, verifying the fix, the render exposed a tenth defect the sweep had only alluded
to: **`introParagraphs.ja` rendered 「机上の要件から 推測するのではなく」**. JSX drops a
newline adjacent to a tag but condenses one between two runs of text into a space, and
the paragraph had been wrapped for readability. See `agent/errors.md`; the rule is that
a Japanese JSX fragment may break lines only where they abut a tag.

The visitor counter's `.sr-only` duplicate was reported and deliberately **not**
changed: it is the canonical accessible pattern (the per-character spans are
`aria-hidden`, so assistive tech reads the value once), and duplication in `textContent`
is inherent to every use of visually-hidden text. Only the missing space was a defect.

Consequences: 28 route × locale × breakpoint combos re-swept — zero problems, zero
console errors, zero responses >= 400, `lang` correct per locale, badges Japanese under
`ja`, no em dash in any rendered string, no overflow or clipped titles, all flow-chart
connectors present, and every diamond label still passing the strict `isPointInFill`
corner test after "Graded by the teacher model" widened it. The mobile expand still
writes the tapped card's exact rect and closes clean (ADR-051 holds). A dedicated scan
for ASCII spaces adjacent to CJK now comes back with only the legitimate cases.
Production build clean.

Not covered by this pass, and worth a look sometime: the resume PDFs, the strings inside
the raster project screenshots, and colour contrast of the small grey type.

units.title: ADR-054 — The open animation's real defects, and two contribution-window bugs (2026-08-02)
units.content:
# ADR-054 — The open animation's real defects, and two contribution-window bugs (2026-08-02)

Context: the user reported, repeatedly, that opening a project "glitches out — it's
displaced, it's supposed to be shown immediately up top, it shows down and then up at
the top within a split second." Earlier passes had fixed the overlay's *origin*
(ADR-051) but never the content's behaviour once the box was moving. Two diagnostic
subagents measured the desktop and mobile paths per animation frame over CDP.

### What was actually wrong

**Desktop.** Every `.pd-animate` element was painted 26px below its resting position
from the first visible frame, and the `.from()` was positioned `'-=0.12'` with a 0.07
stagger — so the panel was fully opaque at ~290ms while its content was still sliding
until ~1130ms. Content demonstrably arrived low and travelled up long after the panel
was solid. That is the reported symptom, by design rather than by accident.

Underneath it sat a genuine bug. `.pd-back` carries `transition: ... transform 160ms`
for its `:hover { transform: translateX(-2px) }` nudge. GSAP's `.from()` initialises
lazily when the playhead reaches it; by then the CSS transition had already carried the
computed transform partway, GSAP read that in-flight value as the element's *resting*
`y`, and baked it in. The button slid **down** ~26px instead of up and stayed there for
the life of the overlay — final inline `translate(0px, 25.574px)`, still present at
t=3000ms, and race-dependent (25.57px at 1280x900, 18.34px at 1440x900). Its gap to the
screenshot rendered ~18px instead of the designed 44px, and its hover nudge was dead,
overridden by GSAP's leftover inline transform.

**Mobile.** Three separate things, in increasing order of how much they matter:
- The box residual: `.project-detail-inner` is a normal-flow child of the element whose
  `top` is being tweened, and `pinnedInnerLayout()` pins only width. `cardExpandEase`
  has covered 95.5% by t=0.22 where the content faded in, leaving 4.5% x `origin.top`
  (4–36px) of upward travel in plain sight.
- **The dominant defect:** the clone and the real page are different layouts. The cloned
  card's title rests **110.3px** above the detail page's `<h1>` and its preview ~90px
  above `.pd-shot`, yet both layers were over 10% opaque for ~200ms — two vertically
  offset copies of the same title and image dissolving through each other.
- Tapping a card whose scroll-reveal `gsap.from(card, {y:36, opacity:0, scale:0.985})`
  was still running snapshotted its in-flight inline styles into `card.outerHTML`. The
  clone then morphed as a featureless black rectangle at `opacity: 0` with its title
  266px out of place, and `measureOrigin()` — which neutralises `main`'s transform but
  not the card's own — returned the scaled box, 344.75x398.68 instead of 350x404.75.

### Decisions

1. **Desktop hero lands in place and only fades.** `.pd-back`, `.pd-shot` and
   `.pd-headline` get opacity only, no `y`. That removes the reported displacement and,
   because GSAP no longer writes a transform to `.pd-back`, it removes the permanent
   offset at its source and gives the hover nudge back to CSS. `.pd-block`s keep a small
   staged rise — they are below the fold, so it is never seen arriving — but via
   `fromTo` rather than `.from()`, so the end value is pinned and no stray CSS
   transition can bake an offset in again.
2. **Mobile hands over instead of cross-fading.** The clone is gone by 0.32 and the real
   content starts after it. `.project-detail` and `.pd-expand-face` share `#0b0d0e`, so
   the handover is invisible, and waiting until 0.32 also drops the box residual to
   under a pixel. Rejected: pinning inner's vertical offset — a subagent verified
   empirically that it puts `.pd-back` 474px above the box's top edge where
   `overflow: hidden` deletes it, and the overflow cannot simply be dropped because the
   real content is ~3000px tall.
3. **Settle the card before snapshotting it.** `gsap.killTweensOf(card)` plus
   `clearProps` before reading `outerHTML`. The card is about to be hidden by
   `is-expand-origin`, and on close it should be at rest — which is what clearProps
   leaves. This also fixes the bad `origin` rect.

### The two contribution-window bugs (carried over from ADR-053)

4. **Weekday alignment.** The grid is seven rows deep flowing column-first, so a column
   only means "one week" if the first cell sits in the row for its own weekday — which a
   flat `slice(-364)` of data ending *today* satisfies one day in seven.

   The first attempt trimmed forward to the next Sunday, and the very next snapshot showed
   why that was wrong: pulled on 2026-08-02 it starts on a **Monday**, so trimming threw
   away six days of history and silently shrank the total. Instead the first cell is now
   offset into its own weekday row (`gridRowStart: leadIn + 1`) and the rest auto-flow from
   there, so column one is partial — which is what GitHub does — and not a single day is
   lost. `weekCount` and every month label's column count from `leadIn` rather than zero.
   Verified by grouping the painted cells by their actual Y: seven rows, each holding
   exactly one weekday, mapping 0..6 in order, with all 364 days retained.
5. **Caption vs grid.** `pickTotal` used the API's `total.lastYear`, computed over its
   whole returned range rather than the range drawn. Simulated across a fortnight of
   dates, the caption disagreed with the grid on **13 days out of 14**. The total is now
   always the sum of the cells on screen. The snapshot's own total already equalled the
   sum of its cells, so nothing changes there.

Consequences, all measured after the change: mobile travel-while-visible **0px** (was
4–36), double-image window **0ms** (was ~200ms), clone-vs-real title gap **0** (was
110.3px), with the box fully landed and the clone gone before content appears. Desktop
back/headline/shot travel **0px** each (was 26), `.pd-back` final transform `none` (was a
permanent `translate(0px, 25.574px)`), inline style just `opacity: 1`, and its gap back
to the designed **44px**. The open still writes the tapped card's exact rect and the
close still lands on it. The grid fix proved itself live: this ran on Sunday 2026-08-02,
exactly the case the old code got wrong, and rendered a correctly weekday-aligned
53-column grid — seven rows, zero rows mixing weekdays, all 364 days kept — with caption
587 equal to the sum of its cells. 28 route x locale x breakpoint combos
clean, 0 console errors, 0 responses >= 400. Production build clean.

   there, so column one is partial — which is what GitHub does — and not a single day is
   lost. `weekCount` and every month label's column count from `leadIn` rather than zero.
   Verified by grouping the painted cells by their actual Y: seven rows, each holding
   exactly one weekday, mapping 0..6 in order, with all 364 days retained.
5. **Caption vs grid.** `pickTotal` used the API's `total.lastYear`, computed over its
   whole returned range rather than the range drawn. Simulated across a fortnight of
   dates, the caption disagreed with the grid on **13 days out of 14**. The total is now
   always the sum of the cells on screen. The snapshot's own total already equalled the
   sum of its cells, so nothing changes there.

Consequences, all measured after the change: mobile travel-while-visible **0px** (was
4–36), double-image window **0ms** (was ~200ms), clone-vs-real title gap **0** (was
110.3px), with the box fully landed and the clone gone before content appears. Desktop
back/headline/shot travel **0px** each (was 26), `.pd-back` final transform `none` (was a
permanent `translate(0px, 25.574px)`), inline style just `opacity: 1`, and its gap back
to the designed **44px**. The open still writes the tapped card's exact rect and the
close still lands on it. The grid fix proved itself live: this ran on Sunday 2026-08-02,
exactly the case the old code got wrong, and rendered a correctly weekday-aligned
53-column grid — seven rows, zero rows mixing weekdays, all 364 days kept — with caption
587 equal to the sum of its cells. 28 route x locale x breakpoint combos
clean, 0 console errors, 0 responses >= 400. Production build clean.

units.title: ADR-055 — Daijin is a desktop-only, time-driven scroll companion (2026-08-14)
units.content:
# ADR-055 — Daijin is a desktop-only, time-driven scroll companion (2026-08-14)

Status: Accepted.

Context: The finished Daijin mascot was built as complete traditional-animation frames in a separate
lab. The portfolio needs the character at the bottom-right without disturbing its dense mobile
layout, inheriting ScrollSmoother transforms, blocking controls, or turning scrolling into choppy
frame scrubbing. Copying all 15 lossless lab clips would also add unnecessary download weight.

Decision: Add `DaijinMascot` outside `#smooth-wrapper` and render a persistent 1024×1024 SVG viewport
over one of nine optimized paired WebP clips. Playback uses elapsed time and `requestAnimationFrame`;
the existing scoped ScrollTrigger only chooses a shuffled, non-repeating clip from progress bands.
Hide the mascot at 760px and below, set `pointer-events:none`, freeze a poster frame for reduced
motion, and unmount it while a project detail is open. Keep the files local under
`public/assets/daijin/` and do not depend on the mascot lab server.

Consequences: The desktop mascot remains anchored to the viewport, changes personality naturally as
the visitor moves through the page, and continues smooth animation between scroll events. Phones pay
no decoded-image or layout cost because CSS hides the component. The selected nine clip pairs add
about 27.3 MB of compressed public assets; future work should retain paired lazy loading and validate
every atlas rather than preloading the full library.

units.title: ADR-056 — Use semantic scenes and an imperative half-scale canvas (2026-08-14)
units.content:
# ADR-056 — Use semantic scenes and an imperative half-scale canvas (2026-08-14)

Status: Accepted; refines ADR-055.

Context: The first portfolio integration decoded two 6144×4096 atlases per active clip, roughly
192 MB of RGBA pixels, and changed React state at up to 24 fps. The animated CSS drop-shadow added
another full transparent-layer filter each frame. Scroll bands selected clips arbitrarily, and a
hard change between independently drawn poses exposed the different body silhouettes.

Decision: Downsample the portfolio copies to 3072×2048 with 512×512 cells, which is still slightly
above 2× the largest CSS display size. Draw crops imperatively into one 512×512 canvas and update only
diagnostic data attributes, not React state. Remove the drop-shadow, decode only the active pair, and
blend the retained old canvas into the new clip over 280ms at section boundaries. Replace arbitrary
bands with semantic scenes: Profile→Playful, Skills→Clever, Experience→Working,
Contributions→Thinking, Projects→Curious, Writing→Listening, and Contact→Happy. Move between a small
profile perch and three right-rail positions with a contained CSS transition.

Consequences: Active decoded memory falls to about 48 MB, the complete portfolio mascot asset set is
12.27 MB, React does no frame-rate work, and the canvas redraws only when the authored frame advances
after the brief transition. Internal clips remain traditional frame animation; only
the boundary between two complete performances blends. Daijin now relates to the content currently
being viewed and phones do not mount or decode the component. New sections must be placed in the scene
map in document order, and atlas copies must remain 3072×2048.

units.title: ADR-057 — Keep one left perch and make section performances one-shot (2026-08-14)
units.content:
# ADR-057 — Keep one left perch and make section performances one-shot (2026-08-14)

Status: Accepted; refines ADR-056.

Context: Moving Daijin from the profile to high/middle/low right-rail positions made the mascot feel
detached from the page. The long vertical travel was visible during scrolling, and looping a new clip
for an entire section read as a background GIF rather than a character reacting. A short clip blend
did not solve the spatial mismatch.

Decision: Keep the mascot fixed at one clamped top-left coordinate, overlapping the profile photo and
remaining on the left for the whole desktop visit. Measure section thresholds so their headings
scroll up to that perch. Trigger one complete contextual clip per crossing, clamp non-Idle playback at
frame 46, then use a React effect keyed by clip and scene to return to looping Idle. Give SectionTitle
stable `data-daijin-title` partner hooks and play one restrained elastic nudge when Skills, Work,
Projects, or Thoughts reaches Daijin; nudge the Contribution block and Contact heading similarly.
During the profile Playful action, apply a one-shot CSS keyframe that rotates the photo shell left,
right, and back to rest. Disable the photo keyframe under reduced motion.

Consequences: Daijin has a stable spatial relationship with the portrait and never slides vertically
or crosses to the right. Reactions read as discrete performances with a clear start and finish, can
retrigger when scrolling back, and remain independent of scroll velocity. Partner selectors and scene
order are now part of the interaction contract; adding a heading requires both its data hook and scene
entry. Idle remains the only intentional infinite clip.

units.title: ADR-058 — Reserve a mascot header gap instead of overlapping content (2026-08-14)
units.content:
# ADR-058 — Reserve a mascot header gap instead of overlapping content (2026-08-14)

Status: Accepted; refines ADR-057.

Context: A 132px fixed mascot at top 10px extended to y=142 while the profile photo began near y=70.
The deliberate overlap covered the portrait and, while scrolling, put Daijin directly on top of the
section title. This looked crowded at both full desktop and the narrower split-browser width.

Decision: Reduce Daijin to 112×112 and increase desktop main top padding from 58px to 132px. Keep the
mascot at top 10px, the semantic section trigger at top 150px, and the existing <=760px main padding
of 46px because the mascot is not mounted there.

Consequences: At 1280px, Daijin ends at y=122 and the portrait begins at y=142, producing a measured
20px clear gap. Titles meet the perch around y=150–155, producing 28–33px of breathing room while
remaining close enough for the nudge interaction to read. The extra desktop header height is now part
of the mascot layout contract.

units.title: ADR-059 — Use a responsive left rail and exclude the Playful turnaround (2026-08-14)
units.content:
# ADR-059 — Use a responsive left rail and exclude the Playful turnaround (2026-08-14)

Status: Accepted; supersedes ADR-057's Idle handoff and ADR-058's above-content gap.

Context: The above-image perch still did not match the intended composition: Daijin belongs beside
the portrait and beside each section title. Canvas bounds also overstated the visual reach because
the sprite contains transparent padding. More importantly, Playful's source sheet contains a
malformed generated in-between and an unwanted back-view turn, so playing all 46 frames created the
reported spin/glitch even after the Idle transition was removed.

Decision: Restore the original desktop top padding and reserve a responsive left rail. Use a
profile-only horizontal inset so the drawn paw crosses the portrait edge, while non-profile scenes
use the wider heading coordinate. Extend the card-rock keyframe to 3.2 seconds. Give Playful an
explicit front-facing frame path (9 through 23, then back to 9), decode only sheet A for that path,
and hold the final selected frame. Do not automatically transition contextual clips to Idle.

Consequences: Daijin now reads as physically beside the current element, touches the photo during the
reach, and never displays the corrupted turn or back-view frames. The portrait uses a deliberate
overlap while headings retain breathing room. Clip-specific frame paths are now part of the renderer
contract and can exclude bad source passages without regenerating the atlas.

units.title: A media query that changes `.
units.content:
# A media query that changes `.

- A media query that changes `.experience-summary`'s negative margin and one that changes `.dot`'s `left` are coupled: the dot offset is `lineCentre - itemLeft + summaryOverhang - 8`. The `<=760px` block set `left: -25.5px` (the no-overhang value) while the overhang was still 12px until `<=560px`, so every dot sat 12px off the line for that whole band and nobody noticed because the two checked breakpoints (desktop and 375px) both happened to be correct. When touching either rule, measure at 700px as well — and prefer `offsetLeft` chains over `getBoundingClientRect()`, since a frozen GSAP `scale(0)` collapses the rect but leaves layout position intact.

units.title: `background-clip: text` clips to the glyphs of the element it is set on, so a shimmer must live on i
units.content:
# `background-clip: text` clips to the glyphs of the element it is set on, so a shimmer must live on i

- `background-clip: text` clips to the glyphs of the element it is set on, so a shimmer must live on its own span — putting it on a flex parent would also blank any non-text sibling via the inherited transparent `-webkit-text-fill-color`. Always pair it with a `background-color` in the base tone: that is clipped to the glyphs too and keeps the text legible if the gradient ever fails to paint, instead of leaving it invisible.

units.title: BorderBeam's own `overflow: hidden` on `[data-beam]` does not reliably clip its blurred glow layer (
units.content:
# BorderBeam's own `overflow: hidden` on `[data-beam]` does not reliably clip its blurred glow layer (

- BorderBeam's own `overflow: hidden` on `[data-beam]` does not reliably clip its blurred glow layer (`filter: blur()` child) in this engine — a filter-vs-overflow-clip compositing quirk. The bloom bled a colored smear past the avatar's rounded corner (worst on mobile, bottom-left). Fix: add `contain: paint` to `.avatar-beam` — stronger than `overflow: hidden`, forces every descendant (filtered or not) to clip to the box.

units.title: Chrome's `--headless --screenshot --virtual-time-budget=N` fast-forwards timers, which breaks Fireba
units.content:
# Chrome's `--headless --screenshot --virtual-time-budget=N` fast-forwards timers, which breaks Fireba

- Chrome's `--headless --screenshot --virtual-time-budget=N` fast-forwards timers, which breaks Firebase auth initialisation and captures SPAs on their "Loading…" frame. For a real screenshot, drive the DevTools protocol instead: `Page.navigate` → wait for `Page.loadEventFired` → settle a few seconds → `Page.captureScreenshot`, with `Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride` at `deviceScaleFactor: 2` for the 1440x810 preview convention.

units.title: `ContributionGrid` cells use `key={day.
units.content:
# `ContributionGrid` cells use `key={day.

- `ContributionGrid` cells use `key={day.date || index}`. Fallback synthetic data and the real snapshot/API data commonly share recent date-string keys, so React reuses those DOM nodes across the swap instead of remounting — which means the cell-reveal ScrollTrigger's cached trigger position (measured against the fallback layout, before real data changed the section's height) never gets recalculated, and cells can be stuck permanently at their `opacity:0` "from" state. The existing `window.load` -> `ScrollTrigger.refresh()` doesn't cover this because the fetch typically resolves after `load` fires. Fix: refresh inside `ContributionGrid` in a `useEffect` keyed on `[cells, total]`, so it re-fires whenever the real data replaces the fallback.

# `element.

units.title: `getBoundingClientRect()` returns the **post-transform** box.
units.content:
# `getBoundingClientRect()` returns the **post-transform** box.

- `getBoundingClientRect()` returns the **post-transform** box. While the project overlay is open, `main` sits at `scale(0.95)`, so measuring the origin card during the close returned its scaled rect and the close animated to a target 53px too high and 17px too narrow. `measureOrigin()` now neutralises `main`'s inline transform for the measurement and restores it (reading a rect forces layout but never a paint, so nothing flashes). Never use `getBoundingClientRect` to answer "where will this be once the transforms finish" (ADR-047).

units.title: **JSX turns a mid-text line break into a space, which is wrong in Japanese.
units.content:
# **JSX turns a mid-text line break into a space, which is wrong in Japanese.

- **JSX turns a mid-text line break into a space, which is wrong in Japanese.** Babel drops a newline that sits next to a tag but condenses one that falls between two runs of text into a single space. `introParagraphs.ja` was wrapped for readability and rendered 「机上の要件から 推測するのではなく」 and 「エンジニアに なりたいと」. Japanese takes no inter-word spaces, so a JA JSX fragment must break lines only where they abut a tag, or not at all. Detect it by walking every rendered text node and flagging an ASCII space with a CJK character on either side — that scan also has to whitelist the legitimate cases already on this page: spaced separators (`React + Tailwind / 日英`, `フルスタック開発 / AIエージェント`), `東海大学 情報通信学部`, date ranges (`2023年6月 - 現在`), spacing around Latin numerals (`直近12か月で 586 件`), and `Title: 詳細を見る` aria-labels.

units.title: `ProjectFlowChart`'s connector arrows (`.
units.content:
# `ProjectFlowChart`'s connector arrows (`.

- `ProjectFlowChart`'s connector arrows (`.fc-edge`) were completely invisible — not dim, not miscolored, literally not rendered. Root cause: every connector is a perfectly axis-aligned line (`M x y L x y2` or `M x y H x2`), so its SVG bounding box has zero width or zero height. The `#fc-sketch` hand-drawn-wobble filter used the SVG default `filterUnits="objectBoundingBox"`, whose `x/y/width/height` are percentages of that bounding box — a percentage of zero is zero, so the filter region collapsed to a degenerate rect and the browser rendered nothing for any element using it. The boxes/diamonds have real bounding boxes so they were fine; only zero-area shapes (straight lines) broke. Fix: `filterUnits="userSpaceOnUse"` with a fixed pixel region sized to the SVG's own `width`/`height` (plus margin), so the filter region no longer depends on the filtered element's own bbox. General rule: never leave an `objectBoundingBox` filter (the default) on an element that can have a zero-width or zero-height bounding box — switch to `userSpaceOnUse` with an explicit region instead.

units.content:
# `.

- `.avatar-shell` (sizes the border beam) and `.avatar` (sizes the visible photo) must never be resized independently — if only one gets a breakpoint override, the beam traces a box that no longer matches the photo, producing an offset/drifted glow on that breakpoint (exactly what happened at <=760px: `.avatar` shrank to 108px but `.avatar-shell` stayed at 120x124). Fix: `.avatar` and `.avatar-beam` are always `width:100%; height:100%;` and only `.avatar-shell` carries pixel sizes, so there is one sizing authority per breakpoint, not two that can drift apart.

units.title: The contribution grid's month header only means anything if a grid column is a week.
units.content:
# The contribution grid's month header only means anything if a grid column is a week.

- The contribution grid's month header only means anything if a grid column is a week. While the grid flowed row-major in 35-day rows, the labels were decoration sitting above unrelated days. units.title: The `#fc-sketch` turbulence/displacement filter that was supposed to give the flow chart a hand-draw
units.content:
# The `#fc-sketch` turbulence/displacement filter that was supposed to give the flow chart a hand-draw

- The `#fc-sketch` turbulence/displacement filter that was supposed to give the flow chart a hand-drawn wobble was **invisible**: filtered and `filter: none` renders came out pixel-identical at 3.2x magnification (max channel delta 0). `baseFrequency 0.02` varies over ~50-unit periods and `scale 2.4` displaces by at most ~1 unit, which rounds away at the rendered scale. The chain worked — swapping in `feGaussianBlur stdDeviation=6` blurred everything, and `scale=18` crinkled it visibly. General rule: a displacement filter subtle enough not to look noisy is usually subtle enough to be invisible; do hand-drawn looks as perturbed path geometry, not as a post-process filter. Removed in ADR-044.

units.title: The in-app Browser pane can stop repainting entirely (screenshots come back solid black, `computer`
units.content:
# The in-app Browser pane can stop repainting entirely (screenshots come back solid black, `computer`

- The in-app Browser pane can stop repainting entirely (screenshots come back solid black, `computer` actions time out with "The Browser pane is currently hidden"). DOM measurement via `javascript_exec` keeps working when this happens — fall back to it rather than concluding the page is broken. Related: because `document.hidden` is true, `requestAnimationFrame` never fires, so GSAP timelines never complete and any `onComplete` (for example the detail overlay's unmount) never runs. To exercise rAF-dependent app code, shim `window.requestAnimationFrame` onto `setTimeout` before triggering it; GSAP's own ticker captured the real rAF at load and will stay frozen regardless.

units.content:
# The in-app Browser preview reports `document.

- The in-app Browser preview reports `document.hidden === true`, so `requestAnimationFrame` never fires: GSAP entrance tweens, CSS-driven beams and canvas orbs all freeze at their start state. Verify motion-dependent work by forcing end states in JS (`el.style.opacity='1'; el.style.transform='none'`) or by measuring geometry — do not conclude a rendering bug from a frozen frame.

units.title: The mobile card-expand transition cannot be verified in the preview pane at all: `document.
units.content:
# The mobile card-expand transition cannot be verified in the preview pane at all: `document.

- The mobile card-expand transition cannot be verified in the preview pane at all: `document.hidden` is true there, so `requestAnimationFrame` never fires and GSAP timelines never advance past their first `set`. Four separate ADRs "verified" this animation with synthetic clicks and all of them missed a 171.9px title shift. To actually observe it, drive headless Chrome over CDP at a mobile viewport with `Emulation.setTouchEmulationEnabled`, tap with `Input.dispatchTouchEvent`, and record with `Page.startScreencast` plus a per-`rAF` geometry sampler. The scripts are in the session scratchpad (`record-open.mjs`, `record-close.mjs`, `probe-clone.mjs`).

units.content:
# The mobile detail overlay's `.

- The mobile detail overlay's `.pd-back` and `.pd-headline` carried both `pd-animate` and `pd-reveal`, while `.pd-shot` (the hero image) only ever carried `pd-animate`. `pd-reveal` elements are set to `{y:18, opacity:0}` and only tweened in later (stagger starting at t=0.25 in the open timeline), so the image appeared immediately while the back button and title popped in ~0.25s afterward — read as the header "settling"/glitching up and down after the image loaded. units.title: The project-card mobile expand/collapse animation measured its origin card's `getBoundingClientRect(
units.content:
# The project-card mobile expand/collapse animation measured its origin card's `getBoundingClientRect(

- The project-card mobile expand/collapse animation measured its origin card's `getBoundingClientRect()` once at click time and stored plain numbers, then read them again later inside a `useGSAP` effect that only runs after `window.location.hash` triggers an async `hashchange` -> state update -> re-render round trip. GSAP ScrollSmoother's touch-flick momentum can still be settling the list during that gap — invisible to a synthetic click (which is instant), but reliably reproducible on a real phone flick-then-tap. Fix: re-measure the live card (`detailOriginCardRef.current.getBoundingClientRect()`) at the moment each animation (open AND close) actually builds, instead of trusting a stale click-time snapshot.

units.title: Vite 8 bundles rolldown, which needs Node `^20.
units.content:
# Vite 8 bundles rolldown, which needs Node `^20.

- Vite 8 bundles rolldown, which needs Node `^20.19.0 || >=22.12.0`. The default `node` on this machine is 20.11.0, so every Vite command fails with `SyntaxError: ... 'node:util' does not provide an export named 'styleText'`. Use `PATH=/opt/homebrew/bin:$PATH` (Node 25) or `nvm use`.

units.content:
# `vite dev` does not run Vercel serverless functions, so anything under `api/` is simply absent local

- `vite dev` does not run Vercel serverless functions, so anything under `api/` is simply absent locally. `vite.config.js` carries a dev-only (`apply: 'serve'`) middleware mocking `/api/visits`; add one for any future route or its UI cannot be tested without deploying.

units.title: When judging rendering quality, do not trust the un-magnified preview pane.
units.content:
# When judging rendering quality, do not trust the un-magnified preview pane.

- When judging rendering quality, do not trust the un-magnified preview pane. Capture a clipped, magnified screenshot over CDP (`Page.captureScreenshot` with a `clip` and `scale: 3`) and diff the variants with Pillow — that is what turned "the drawing feels off" into a measurable zero-delta finding.

units.title: When verifying GSAP/ScrollTrigger-driven UI in the Browser preview pane, `scrollIntoView()`/`window.
units.content:
# When verifying GSAP/ScrollTrigger-driven UI in the Browser preview pane, `scrollIntoView()`/`window.

- When verifying GSAP/ScrollTrigger-driven UI in the Browser preview pane, `scrollIntoView()`/`window.scrollTo()` calls made via `javascript_exec` do NOT reliably drive ScrollSmoother/ScrollTrigger the way a real scroll gesture does — some triggers never fire even though the element is visually in view. Use the `computer` tool's real `scroll` action (or a real click/tap) to test scroll-triggered reveals, not JS-dispatched scroll/scrollIntoView.

units.title: `window.
units.content:
# `window.

- `window.history.length > 1` does not mean the previous history entry belongs to this site; it only means the tab has history. Never use it to decide whether `history.back()` is safe — track whether the app itself pushed the entry.

units.title: 2026-07-06 (mobile polish + signature/perf, ADR-023): Added breathing room between the skills marque
units.content:
# 2026-07-06 (mobile polish + signature/perf, ADR-023): Added breathing room between the skills marque

- 2026-07-06 (mobile polish + signature/perf, ADR-023): Added breathing room between the skills marquees and Work Experience (`.skills-marquees` margin-bottom 1px→26px). Brightened the dashed box borders (#444→#56595d) so project card left/right edges are visible on OLED phones. Tech tags now a `repeat(3, auto)` grid everywhere → always a balanced 3+2 (never orphaned 4+1). "Let's Connect" links become a 2×2 grid at ≤470px (flex row on desktop). units.title: 2026-07-06 (signature redesign, ADR-021): Replaced the filled Great Vibes signature with a single-st
units.content:
# 2026-07-06 (signature redesign, ADR-021): Replaced the filled Great Vibes signature with a single-st

- 2026-07-06 (signature redesign, ADR-021): Replaced the filled Great Vibes signature with a single-stroke "hello"-style monoline of "Mohamed Fuad" — Hershey Script (a rounded connected single-line/centre-line font), rendered as one continuous `stroke` path (no fill) where a flat baseline flows in from the left edge, rises into the name, and flows back out to the right, ending in a red period-dot. Generated offline from the SVG font (scratchpad `build-v3.mjs`). `signature-path.js` now exports `signatureViewBox`/`signaturePath`/`signatureDot`/`signatureStrokeWidth` (no more `signatureBaseline`); stroke width is set via the JS-driven `strokeWidth` attribute (NOT CSS, which would override it). DrawSVG draws the whole path as one gesture, then the dot pops. Verified in-browser: renders, animates, no console errors.

units.content:
# 2026-07-06 (signature tracing loop, ADR-022): Removed the red period-dot; added a perpetual glowing

# 2026-07-25 (dependency refresh + eight fixes, ADR-032.

- 2026-07-25 (dependency refresh + eight fixes, ADR-032..036): Updated every dependency to latest (React 19.2.8, Vite 8.1.5, lucide-react 1.26.0, @vitejs/plugin-react 6.0.4) and added `border-beam` + `thinking-orbs`. All external links carry `rel="noopener noreferrer"`. Production build clean.

units.title: 2026-07-26 (avatar glow offset, bio split, real mobile card-expand bug, Excalidraw flow chart — ADR-
units.content:
# 2026-07-26 (avatar glow offset, bio split, real mobile card-expand bug, Excalidraw flow chart — ADR- - 2026-07-26 (avatar glow offset, bio split, real mobile card-expand bug, Excalidraw flow chart — ADR-038/039): Fixed a real mobile-only bug the user caught: the border beam's glow was visibly offset from the avatar because `.avatar` had its own hardcoded breakpoint size never mirrored onto `.avatar-shell` (which sizes the beam) — now `.avatar`/`.avatar-beam` always fill `.avatar-shell`, the single sizing authority. Split the bio into two `

` (`introParagraphs`, both locales). Found and fixed the actual cause of the still-recurring mobile card-expand glitch: the origin card's rect was captured once at click time and reused later inside a `useGSAP` effect that only fires after an async hash-change round trip — during that gap, GSAP ScrollSmoother's touch-flick momentum can still be moving the list on a real phone (invisible to any synthetic click, which is why it kept passing verification). Fixed by re-measuring the live card fresh at the moment each open/close animation actually builds. Rebuilt `ProjectFlowChart` to match the user's reference design exactly: self-hosted Excalidraw's own "Excalifont" hand-drawn typeface (`public/fonts/Excalifont-Regular.woff2`, MIT/self-hosting-documented package, no new runtime dependency), Excalidraw's default color palette per stage kind via a `--fc-tone` CSS var, more rounded corners, and a shared `#fc-sketch` SVG filter for a hand-drawn wobble on every shape/edge (not text). Verified zero overflow/overlap across all four projects at both flowchart geometries, and the card-expand fix with a real scroll-then-immediately-tap sequence. Production build clean.

units.title: 2026-07-26 (flow chart connector lines invisible, ADR-041): The user reported the system-architectur
units.content:
# 2026-07-26 (flow chart connector lines invisible, ADR-041): The user reported the system-architectur

- 2026-07-26 (flow chart connector lines invisible, ADR-041): The user reported the system-architecture flow chart's connecting lines were not visible at all. Confirmed via `getBBox()` on the live `.fc-edge` paths: every connector is a straight axis-aligned line, so its bounding box has zero width or zero height — and the shared `#fc-sketch` hand-drawn-wobble filter used the SVG default `objectBoundingBox` units, whose region is a percentage of that box. A percentage of zero is zero, so the filter region collapsed to nothing and every connector line silently failed to render (boxes/diamonds were unaffected since they have real bounding boxes). Fixed by switching `#fc-sketch` to `filterUnits="userSpaceOnUse"` with an explicit pixel region sized to the chart's own SVG dimensions. Verified live at both 375px and desktop widths: every connector line and arrowhead now renders with its label, no console errors, clean production build.

units.title: 2026-07-26 (mobile detail header desync fix, ADR-040): The user reported the mobile project-detail o
units.content:
# 2026-07-26 (mobile detail header desync fix, ADR-040): The user reported the mobile project-detail o

- 2026-07-26 (mobile detail header desync fix, ADR-040): The user reported the mobile project-detail overlay still glitched on open after the ADR-038 origin-measurement fix — the hero image appeared, then the back button and title visibly popped in afterward, reading as an "up and down" settle. Root cause: `.pd-back` and `.pd-headline` carried both `pd-animate` and `pd-reveal`, while `.pd-shot` (the image) only ever carried `pd-animate` — so the header sat on the delayed, staggered `pd-reveal` track (tween starts at t=0.25 in the open timeline) while the image rendered immediately. Fixed by dropping `pd-reveal` from `.pd-back`/`.pd-headline` so all three appear together; `.pd-block` sections (below the fold) intentionally kept their stagger. Verified live at 375px width: `.pd-back`/`.pd-headline`/`.pd-shot` all read `className` without `pd-reveal` and all sit at `opacity:1` together at the same instant, no console errors. Production build clean.

units.title: 2026-07-26 (real mobile bugs found + fixed, ADR-037): The previous session's mobile check missed two
units.content:
# 2026-07-26 (real mobile bugs found + fixed, ADR-037): The previous session's mobile check missed two

- 2026-07-26 (real mobile bugs found + fixed, ADR-037): The previous session's mobile check missed two genuine bugs, caught this session via real scroll/tap testing instead of JS-dispatched scroll. (1) The border beam's blurred glow bled past the avatar's rounded corner (BorderBeam's own overflow:hidden doesn't reliably clip a filtered child in this engine) — fixed with `contain: paint` on `.avatar-beam`. (2) The entire Work Experience list and every contribution-grid cell rendered permanently invisible on load — caused by `ContributionGrid`'s cells sharing `key={day.date}` between fallback and real data, so React reused DOM nodes across the swap and the cell-reveal ScrollTrigger's cached position (from before real data changed the layout) never refreshed; fixed with a `useEffect(() => ScrollTrigger.refresh(), [cells, total])`. Re-verified experience-card tap-to-expand, the mobile project-open animation, and both flow charts on mobile — all clean. Production build passed.

units.title: 2026-07-29 (close-animation target, shimmer heading, visitor counter — ADR-047/048): Recording the m
units.content:
# 2026-07-29 (close-animation target, shimmer heading, visitor counter — ADR-047/048): Recording the m

- 2026-07-29 (close-animation target, shimmer heading, visitor counter — ADR-047/048): Recording the mobile **close** surfaced a second bug independent of ADR-046: the overlay animated back to `[30, 130, 333, 385]` while the card sits at `[20, 183, 350, 405]`. Cause — `main` is left at `scale(0.95)` while the overlay is open, and `getBoundingClientRect()` reports the post-transform box, so the close aimed at the card's scaled rect (350x0.95=332.5, 405x0.95=384.8, matching the measurements exactly). `measureOrigin()` now neutralises the transform for the measurement; the close lands within 0.2px on every axis. Added the two transitions.dev treatments the user asked for, with parameters read off the live demos rather than guessed: **shimmer text** on "Building AI agent tools" (underline removed; gradient clipped to the glyphs sweeping `background-position` 100%→0%, with a solid `background-color` fallback so the text can never render invisible, and dropped entirely under reduced motion), and a **footer visitor counter** using the "Number pop-in" animation — 500ms, `cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.45, 0.64, 1)`, 70ms stagger, 8px rise, 2px blur, verified as 66-67ms measured stagger with the expected -0.5px spring overshoot. It replays on every scroll into view and again whenever the value changes. The count comes from a new `api/visits.mjs` Vercel function backed by Upstash Redis, with uniqueness enforced server-side via `SET NX EX` on a truncated salted hash of IP+UA rather than trusting the browser. The counter is optional by design: `useVisitorCount` yields `null` on any failure and the footer omits it, verified with the endpoint blocked at the network layer. Needs `UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL` and `UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_TOKEN` in Vercel before it appears.

units.title: 2026-07-29 (flow-chart drawing quality, ADR-044): The user asked why the system-architecture diagram
units.content:
# 2026-07-29 (flow-chart drawing quality, ADR-044): The user asked why the system-architecture diagram

- 2026-07-29 (flow-chart drawing quality, ADR-044): The user asked why the system-architecture diagram did not look clean — "not the straight lines alone, but the drawing itself." Captured the chart at 3.2x over CDP with the `#fc-sketch` hand-drawn filter on and forced off, and diffed: **pixel-identical, max channel delta 0.** The filter chain worked (a blur primitive blurred everything; `scale=18` crinkled it) but at `baseFrequency 0.02` / `scale 2.4` it displaced by at most ~1 user unit and rounded away entirely. The chart was therefore machine-perfect geometry wearing a handwriting font, which is exactly what read as "not clean", while costing 13 chart-sized filter buffers per paint. Removed the filter and committed to a precise diagram: rounded joins and caps, non-scaling strokes, connectors lightened to 1.5 against the shapes' 2 so the boxes lead, arrowheads matched to their line, and subtitles mixed 45% toward the page text colour because the raw Excalidraw tone was barely legible on near-black. Also removed the "By the numbers" strip from the Internship Portal page at the user's request (kept on AI Brain), re-shot the AI Brain preview at a 2048x1152 logical viewport so the frame is filled with dashboard rather than empty space, and trimmed two Japanese branch labels that had no margin in the 116-unit phone box. Verified all six charts in EN and JA at 375px and 1280px; production build clean.

units.title: 2026-07-29 (mobile expand glitch found by recording it, ADR-046): The user reported the mobile proje
units.content:
# 2026-07-29 (mobile expand glitch found by recording it, ADR-046): The user reported the mobile proje

- 2026-07-29 (mobile expand glitch found by recording it, ADR-046): The user reported the mobile project-open still "realigns a bit". Recorded it properly for the first time — headless Chrome at 390x844 with touch emulation, a real dispatched tap, `Page.startScreencast`, and a per-`rAF` geometry sampler — because the preview pane freezes `rAF` and every earlier verification of this animation (ADR-029/036/038/040) had been done with synthetic clicks against a frozen timeline. Cause: `.pd-expand-face .project { width: 100% }` sizes the cloned card as a percentage of the overlay, and the overlay's width is exactly what the open tweens, so the clone re-laid out every frame — its grid column went 306→338→350px, its preview image drifted 33.6px wider, and **its title slid 171.9px down the screen**. Fixed with `pinnedFaceLayout(origin)` on the clone in both the open and close timelines, the same treatment ADR-036 gave `.project-detail-inner`. Note GSAP defaults `minHeight` to percent, not px — the first attempt wrote `min-height: 404.75%` and made the clone 3121px tall, so the helper returns explicit px strings. After the fix every clone child matches its original exactly and drift is 0.0px in width, height and title position across all three cards tested, open and close. Production build clean.

units.content:
# 2026-07-29 (repo-wide bug sweep, ADR-042): Pulled four automated snapshot commits, then audited the

- 2026-07-29 (repo-wide bug sweep, ADR-042): Pulled four automated snapshot commits, then audited the whole repo and fixed everything found. Layout: timeline dots were 12px off the dashed line for the entire 561-760px band (the `<=760px` `.dot` offset assumed a negative summary margin that does not apply until `<=560px`), and at `<=470px` the project title and Live/GitHub buttons were centred over a left-aligned card because the stacked heading inherited `align-items: center`. The contribution grid was rebuilt from a 35-column row-major block of 245 days into 52 week-columns x 7 rows covering a real 12 months, with month labels anchored to the week each month starts in — previously the nine evenly-spaced labels sat above days they had nothing to do with, and the caption claimed 12 months over ~8 months of data. Behaviour: "Back to projects" used `history.length > 1` and could send a visitor who arrived from a shared link straight back off the site; the detail overlay declared `role="dialog" aria-modal="true"` while Escape did nothing, focus never entered it, and 33 background controls stayed tabbable. Both fixed, with focus deferred until the entrance tween actually makes the overlay visible. Toolchain: added `.nvmrc` + `engines` (Node 20.11 on this machine fails every Vite 8 command), added the missing `vite.config.js` so the dev server finally has Fast Refresh, guarded `createRoot` against HMR re-entry, moved build deps to `devDependencies`, dropped the unused `qrcode`, and marked the package private. Content and robustness: the Japanese CV was a byte-identical copy of the English one and has been replaced with the real 履歴書・職務経歴書 supplied by the user, restoring the locale-aware résumé link, the stale hardcoded `561` fallback total is now derived from the data, an error boundary plus a date-shape filter keep one malformed API row from blanking the page, Japanese-locale screen-reader strings are localized, CDN icon URLs are pinned with an `onError` fallback, and 16 unused images (~916 KB) were deleted. README drift corrected along the way (React 18 -> 19, Codex Account Switcher -> ClaudeShot, a `qrcode` dependency the site never used). Verified by measurement at 320/375/400/561/700/760/761/1280px in both locales; production build clean.

# 2026-07-29 (two current projects added, ADR-043): Researched the user's two active repos and added t

Also fixed TokaiHub's live URL, which still pointed at GitHub Pages. Verified in EN and JA at 375px and 1280px; production build clean.

units.content:
# 2026-07-30 (pull + verify, then human-voiced project copy — ADR-049): Pulled `f18f507`, an automated

- 2026-07-30 (pull + verify, then human-voiced project copy — ADR-049): Pulled `f18f507`, an automated contribution snapshot (total 582 → 583, today's cell 0 → 1); nothing else had changed and the tree was clean. Verified install, production build, and the running site: all requests 200, no console errors, no broken images, total renders 583, six cards in order, no horizontal overflow at 390px or 1280px, timeline dots 0.0px off the dashed line, five tech chips on one line per card. Two testing artifacts worth not re-diagnosing: resizing the preview viewport *after* load leaves `.project-shot-hint` reading `opacity: 0` even though the `≤760px` rule applies on a fresh load at the same width, and the pane freezes rAF outright (**0 ticks in 12.2s**), which is why every scroll-revealed block reads `opacity: 0` there. Neither is a site bug. Then, on the user's request, rewrote the **Internship Portal** and **AI Brain Platform** copy: deleted both `status` blocks (that is where "In active development", "The web app is live", "The iOS client" and "Ongoing research" all lived), stripped every em dash from both projects in both locales, and rewrote overview, features and flow into the plain first-person voice WebDrop already used. The Internship Portal is no longer described as a "LaTeX-to-PDF compiler" — it now leads with searching the postings and tracking an application from saved to interview, with the résumé editor demoted to the last bullet and the system map changed to Find / Track / Your data / Shared server. "Paid work" and "etc." were also named by the user but do not exist anywhere in the source. Verified over CDP in headless Chrome (the only way to see the reveals) across both breakpoints, both slugs and both locales; production build clean. The Internship Portal flow chart still shows "Tectonic to PDF" on purpose — see ADR-049. Also fixed the AI Brain diamond's subtitle overhang the same day (ADR-050): `FlowBox` placed a subtitle at `mid + gap` for every shape, which is right for a constant-width rectangle but not for a diamond that has already tapered 36% by that height. A decision's two lines now straddle the midline **and** the subtitle was shortened ("Graded by the teacher" / "教師モデルが採点"), because straddling alone still left the text's lower corners outside the path — the first check of that fix measured the shape's width at the text's centre line and wrongly passed it. All four `getBBox()` corners now test inside via `isPointInFill`, both locales, both geometries.

units.title: 2026-07-30 (validation subagent; mobile expand opened from the wrong corner — ADR-051): A validation
units.content:
# 2026-07-30 (validation subagent; mobile expand opened from the wrong corner — ADR-051): A validation

- 2026-07-30 (validation subagent; mobile expand opened from the wrong corner — ADR-051): A validation subagent swept every route × locale × breakpoint and found a severe pre-existing bug none of ADR-029/036/038/040/046/047 had caught: **the mobile card-expand opened from the viewport's top-left corner, not the tapped card.** `gsap.set(el, { inset: 'auto', left, top, ... })` — GSAP's CSSPlugin prepends its PropTween list, so vars apply in reverse and `inset: 'auto'` wiped `left`/`top`; the tween then started from a computed 0,0 and `left` stayed 0 for all ~80 frames. Start error equalled the card's offset from the viewport origin, up to ~451px. Fixed by setting `right`/`bottom` to auto explicitly instead of the shorthand; the overlay's first style write now matches the card rect exactly. The close was always correct (it never touches `inset`), which is why the asymmetry survived so long — and ADR-046's sampler only compared clone children to their originals, all relative, never the overlay's absolute origin. The same sweep confirmed clean: 0 console errors and 0 responses ≥400 over ~60 loads, no horizontal overflow or clipped text on any of 28 combos, no broken images, 364/364 contribution cells revealing, all flow-chart connectors rendering, and the close landing within 0.42px. It also surfaced open items not yet acted on — see below.

units.title: 2026-08-02 (open-animation glitch finally diagnosed and fixed; contribution window corrected — ADR-0
units.content:
# 2026-08-02 (open-animation glitch finally diagnosed and fixed; contribution window corrected — ADR-0

- 2026-08-02 (open-animation glitch finally diagnosed and fixed; contribution window corrected — ADR-054): Two subagents measured the open per animation frame. **Desktop**: every `.pd-animate` element painted 26px low and was still sliding at ~1130ms while the panel was opaque at ~290ms — plus a real bug where `.pd-back`'s `transition: transform 160ms` (for its hover nudge) swallowed GSAP's lazily-initialised `.from()`, so the button slid *down* ~26px and stayed there permanently (25.57px at 1280, 18.34px at 1440 — a race), leaving its gap ~18px instead of 44px. **Mobile**: the clone and the real page are different layouts whose titles rest 110.3px apart, and both were over 10% opaque for ~200ms, so two offset copies dissolved through each other; on top of that the content rode the box's remaining travel (up to 36px), and tapping a card mid scroll-reveal baked `opacity: 0; transform: translate(0,36px) scale(0.985)` into the clone. Fixed by landing the desktop hero in place (opacity only — which also stops GSAP writing transforms to `.pd-back`), handing over on mobile instead of cross-fading, and settling the card before snapshotting it. Also fixed the two contribution-window issues left open on 2026-08-02: the grid now offsets its first cell into its own weekday row so every column is a real week without discarding any days (trimming to a Sunday was tried first and would have thrown away six days of the very next snapshot, which starts on a Monday), and the caption total is always the sum of the cells drawn (the API's own year total disagreed with the grid on 13 days of 14). Verified: travel 0px everywhere, double-image 0ms, `.pd-back` transform `none` and gap 44px, and the grid fix proved live on a Sunday — the exact case the old code got wrong.

units.title: 2026-08-02 (pull + bug sweep; ten copy defects fixed — ADR-053): Pulled `3403921`, another automated
units.content:
# 2026-08-02 (pull + bug sweep; ten copy defects fixed — ADR-053): Pulled `3403921`, another automated

- 2026-08-02 (pull + bug sweep; ten copy defects fixed — ADR-053): Pulled `3403921`, another automated snapshot — the rolling window slid forward (dropped 2025-08-01/02, appended 07-31 and 08-01), total 583 → 586. **The data and its rendering are correct and needed no change**: 364 cells, exactly 52 weeks, contiguous, first cell a Sunday and last a Saturday, `total` equal to the sum of counts, and all 12 month labels independently re-derived and confirmed sitting over columns that really contain those months, with the trailing one-day Aug 2026 correctly dropped by the `span >= 3` filter. Two latent issues in the **live API** path (not the snapshot, so not what renders first): `normalise()` slices the last 364 days ending *today*, which only starts on a Sunday when today in UTC is a Saturday, and `pickTotal` uses the API's whole-year total while the grid shows only those 364 days — today both agree at 586 because the seven dropped rows happen to be zero. Neither is user-visible (the grid renders no weekday labels), so both were left alone and recorded here. A bug-sweep workflow mostly died on a session limit; its copy dimension survived and its nine findings were verified by hand, then fixed — see ADR-053. Verifying the fix exposed a tenth: JSX condenses a mid-text line break into a space, so the Japanese intro rendered 「机上の要件から 推測するのではなく」. Re-swept 28 combos: zero problems, zero console errors, zero 4xx/5xx, diamonds still passing the strict corner test, mobile expand still landing on the tapped card.

# State (overview)

> Last updated: 2026-08-14 · HEAD: main (see git log)

## Current state summary

The workspace contains a Vite React portfolio inspired by `manixh.dev`, populated with Mohamed Fuad's CV content. It uses a professional headshot with a two-sided LinkedIn QR card, bilingual EN/JA copy, expandable work rows, a live rolling-12-month GitHub contribution grid, GSAP motion, and hash-routed project detail views. A fixed Daijin mascot now acts as a desktop-only section companion from a responsive left rail: it touches and plays with the portrait, then sits left of each active heading with breathing room. It uses an imperative 512×512 canvas and authored atlas frames without rerendering React per frame. Each section triggers one contextual performance and holds without an Idle turnaround. Playful is restricted to the clean front-facing reach frames 9–23–9, skipping the malformed turn/back-view passage. The active assets decode on demand, all 18 optimized files total 12.27 MB, and phones mount no mascot or images. The production build is clean on Node 25. Install and build with pnpm.

units.title: Contextual clips must advance once and hold without transitioning to Idle or starting a second loop.
units.content:
# Contextual clips must advance once and hold without transitioning to Idle or starting a second loop.

- Contextual clips must advance once and hold without transitioning to Idle or starting a second
  loop. Playful is the exception to the full-sheet range: it must sample only frames 9–23–9, never
  the malformed frame 8 or the turn/back-view passage in sheet B. Scroll down/up/down and confirm the same section retriggers. While a section enters,
  its title must have a non-identity transform and return cleanly to `none`; the profile shell must
  rotate through both directions for 3.2s and settle to zero.
